paragraphs: Rav Chanan bar Rava; his father Rava was the earlier one. Yuchasin omitted mention of him, perhaps thinking that he was Rav Chanan bar Abba, which led it to the several errors mentioned in the preceding entry. But Sheerit Yosef lists both among Rav's students, and this is correct, for there are two. Chullin 60b: Rav Chanan bar Rabbah—it should read bar Rava, as in Ein Yaakov—said that the shesuah is a creature of its own. He said to Rav Ashi: Beitzah 30a; this Rav Ashi is the earlier one. Ketubot 21a [source locator כ״א רו׳]: a document issued from Mar Shmuel's court, signed by Rav Anan bar Chiyya and Rav Chanan bar Rabbah; it should read Rava. “Geniva said: thus R. Chanan bar Rava said”—Gittin 31b. Rav Huna said to him. R. Chanan bar Rava said, “Many times I said before Rav”—Rosh Hashanah 22a. Rav Huna told him, “Do not disagree with me”—Eruvin 6a. He taught Chiyya bar Rav before Rav: Shabbat 66a; Yoma 19b. Rav Chanan son of Rav Chisda said to Rav Chisda, etc. He answered, “Thus your mother's father said.” Rashi explains in Chullin: Rav Chanan bar Rabbah (read Rava, says Heilprin), who was Rav Chisda’s father-in-law, for which Rashi cites Asarah Yuchasin. Chullin 63a, near the end; Rav Chisda there speaks in his name. I saw in Kiddushin 81b that Rav Acha bar Abba was his father-in-law; the new Talmud editions give another version, Rav Chanan bar Rava. Rav Chisda said, “I saw the copy of Psalms in Rav Chanan bar Rav’s house, etc.” “Rav Charan bar Rava said”—Pesachim 117a, near the end [source forms retained]. When the nasi died, Rav Chisda told R. Chanan bar Rava, “Overturn a mortar, stand upon it, and display the tearing of your garment”: Elu Megallechin, 22b. It requires investigation how he could command his father-in-law thus. “R. Yochanan said”—Berakhot 58a. Rav was his father-in-law; see Rav Chanan bar Abba above. “Rav said”—Rosh Hashanah 31a. Earlier there: “Rav Anan bar Rava said: Rav said”; the new Talmud editions give another version, Rav Chanan bar Abba. This seems right, since you will not find Anan bar Rava elsewhere in the Talmud; see Rav Anan bar Rava above. Eruvin 5b, near the end: “Rabbi said” is a scribal error and should read “Rav said”; there, 6a, 9a. But that matter in Shabbat 9a has “R. Chama bar Gurya said: Rav said.” “Rav said”—Yevamot 63b, two statements; Bava Batra 91a, several statements; Avodah Zarah 11b, 16a, 39a. Shabbat 33a has Rav Chanan bar Rava, so too Ein Yaakov; that matter in Ketubot 8b has bar Rav, so too Ein Yaakov, but should read bar Rava. “R. Chanan bar Rabbah”—it should read Rava—“said: Rav said”: Sukkah 2b.
